holidays.name: National Hairball Awareness Day
holidays.description: A day dedicated to the slimy, unsettling gift your cat leaves on your favorite rug at 3 a.m. Cat owners are encouraged to brush their felines and learn how to cut down on hairballs.
holidays.origin: Observed unofficially each April 30 by pet lovers and veterinary groups as a way to promote cat grooming and digestive health.
holidays.funFact: The scientific term for a hairball is a 'trichobezoar,' and cats can cough them up thanks to the tiny backward-facing barbs on their tongues that trap loose fur while grooming.

holidays.name: International Jazz Day
holidays.description: A worldwide celebration of jazz with concerts, jam sessions, and educational events in over 190 countries, bringing together musicians and fans to honor improvisation and cool.
holidays.origin: Declared by UNESCO in 2011, with the day championed by jazz legend Herbie Hancock, who serves as a UNESCO Goodwill Ambassador.
holidays.funFact: Each year a different 'Global Host City' is chosen for a major all-star concert, which has been held in places like Paris, New Orleans, Istanbul, and Havana.

holidays.name: National Raisin Day
holidays.description: A day to appreciate the humble dried grape, the shriveled snack that sparks fierce debate in oatmeal cookies. Enjoy them in trail mix, baked goods, or straight from the tiny red box.
holidays.origin: Promoted by raisin growers and snack fans, it recognizes California's raisin industry, which supplies a huge share of the world's raisins.
holidays.funFact: It takes about four pounds of fresh grapes to make just one pound of raisins, and most are dried naturally in the sun on paper trays between the vineyard rows.

holidays.name: Bubble Tea Day
holidays.description: A chewy, slurpable celebration of the Taiwanese drink with tapioca pearls at the bottom. Grab a fat straw and fish for those squishy boba treasures.
holidays.origin: Bubble tea was invented in Taiwan in the 1980s, with two tea shops, Hanlin Tea Room and Chun Shui Tang, both claiming to have created it. Its fans now mark the day with discounts and new flavors.
holidays.funFact: The 'bubbles' in bubble tea are chewy balls made from cassava root starch, and some people call the drink 'boba' after the Taiwanese slang for large pearls.

holidays.name: Honesty Day
holidays.description: A day for telling the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth, even about your coworker's questionable casserole. Participants vow to be straightforward, though tact is highly recommended.
holidays.origin: Created in 1990 by author M. Hirsh Goldberg, who wrote 'The Book of Lies' and wanted people to pause and reflect on the importance of honesty in daily life.
holidays.funFact: Goldberg picked April 30 partly because it falls right after the April Fools' Day season, giving people a chance to come clean after a month of pranks, and it also marks the day George Washington was inaugurated as the first U.S. president in 1789.
